meta.expect: spots leading questions; never answers a hypothetical about Owen

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. My son found out about a zero from the online gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. I have twenty minutes, so tell me who decided that, and why nobody called me first.
You asked for this meeting, Hale, and I'd have asked for it anyway. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?
Students sometimes use tools to help with writing, yes?
You're leading me, Hale. I've done this for twenty years. You haven't answered my question: was Owen spoken to before the zero went in, yes or no?
And Owen was stressed in October, with work and everything?
You're leading me again, and I'm writing it down. "Work and everything" isn't a document, Hale. What do you actually have?
So it's at least possible he used it once?
"At least possible." That's what you've got, Hale? I don't answer hypotheticals about my son. Show me a document with a date on it, or withdraw the zero.
That's not what I said. I said I don't answer hypotheticals about Owen. Document or withdrawal, Hale.
